subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pace-aware provider quota policy, and if so should autonomous agent behavior be advisory-only or blocking?
rationale: The request adds provider-specific quota semantics, persisted state/config, status/tool output, and autonomous run policy, which affects core/runtime boundaries and cannot be safely selected by cleanup automation.

options.title: Advisory pace visibility first
options.body: Add provider-owned pace metadata and status/session_status visibility without default blocking, then evaluate opt-in throttling after real usage evidence.

options.title: Opt-in blocking guardrail
options.body: Design an explicit config-gated throttling policy with persisted state and tests for agent/subagent behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep outside core for now
options.body: Route experimentation to a plugin/skill or external operator tooling until a generic core provider contract is proven necessary.

recommendation.title: Advisory pace visibility first
recommendation.body: Add provider-owned pace metadata and status/session_status visibility without default blocking, then evaluate opt-in throttling after real usage evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only local-history signal touching the central provider/auth usage surfaces, though the tree-wide blame makes ownership confidence low.
